name: Guianese Creole French
confidence_why: 2 independent first-hand sources agree (1 agree, 0 refine), none contradicts

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote: verbatim confirmed in the APiCS survey chapter 52, §3 Phonology (file downloaded now; nothing was held before). (2) Deciding source: a 2013 atlas survey sketch by a language specialist (Pfänder), one unargued sentence; first-hand but not a phonology study. (3) Better descriptions exist and are not yet obtained: Saint-Jacques-Fauquenoy 1972 (structural description incl. phonology), Fauquenoy 1967 (ORSTOM phonology), Jennings & Pfänder 2018 ch. 3, Patzelt 2025 handbook chapter; all print-only or paywalled. Open items downloaded now (Wiesinger 2026 LGMEF fiche; Saint-Quentin 1872) are silent on word stress. (4) Final stress is the expected pattern for a French-lexifier creole and nothing seen contradicts the 'fixed-dominant final' coding; the realistic risk from a fuller source is a refinement (accent described as group/phrase-final rather than lexical), not a different syllable. Hence status
audit.second_reader_evidence: The quotation was checked again: independent. (APiCS Online survey ch. 52 'Guyanais', S. Pfaender; print = Michaelis et al. eds. 2013, Survey vol. 2, 220-228). Stripped text, section '3. Phonology': '.. lateral approximant l j <y> w Word stress is always on the last syllable. An orthography has been proposed and promoted by a group of creolists called GEREC-F..' -> the record's sources[0].text is verbatim, locator = §3 Phonology, sentence directly after Table 3 (Consonants).
